themeDerived.note: A5 (17214:103584) and A10 (17264:29098) are two frames of ONE file and derive to DIFFERENT themes. 12 colour tokens appear in both; 10 identical, 2 differ and those 2 decide it: color/background/primary/bold A5=#3366ff (sanoma-learning) vs A10=#137271 (editorial-suite); color/palette/grey/900 A5=#222222 (sanoma-learning) vs A10=#1d1f20 (editorial-suite). The per-FILE theme hypothesis is FALSIFIED. Theme is a property of the frame's bound variable mode. A10's typography corroborates: design binds heading=Raleway/body=Roboto, which are editorial-suite's --sl-brand-text-new-typeset-fontFamily-* and the faces its Typekit bws3iof ships.

variableModeInvestigation.question: Do A5 and A10 differ because the Figma file defines several variable modes?
variableModeInvestigation.answer: YES - confirmed by probe, not inferred.
evidence: Re-queried A5's frame (17214:103584) in the same session: still color/background/primary/bold=#3366ff, color/palette/grey/900=#222222. Stable, not transient.

DECISIVE: queried node 17264:29099, the 'top nav bar' INSTANCE inside A10's frame. It returns color/background/primary/bold=#137271 and text-new/typeset/fontFamily/heading=Raleway. The equivalent instance in A5's frame resolves the same names to #3366ff and Roboto. Same component, same file, two frames, different resolved values - which is what a variable mode is.
10 of the 12 colour tokens common to both frames are byte-identical; only the 2 that discriminate differ, consistent with mode-variant vs mode-invariant values.
variableModeInvestigation.conclusion: Theme is a property of the FRAME's bound variable mode, not of the file, the page or the team. Both runs are right about their own frame. Derivation must be per frame.
variableModeInvestigation.limitation: get_metadata with no nodeId listed only one top-level page ('Cover'), and get_variable_defs on a page id returned 'You currently have nothing selected'. So the mode could not be read as a named property - only its effect, which is unambiguous.

reachedPastPublicApi: sl-tab-group's selected indicator is not exposed as a ::part(), so its colour is set by retargeting --sl-color-border-selected on the element (the same reach-through A5 reported on this component).
sl-form-field's label colour comes from the theme and needed a scoped override to reach --a10-color-chrome.
sl-button exposes no part for its link-fill label colour, so Edit/Delete bind --sl-color-foreground-plain on the element.
table-footer restates the disabled arrow colour explicitly because an outer-tree ::part() declaration WINS over button.css's own `button:is(:disabled)` rule - see cssPartSpecificityHazard.

cssPartSpecificityHazard.finding: A ::part() declaration written in the OUTER tree beats the component's own internal rule for the same property, regardless of the inner rule's specificity. Shadow-part styles from the host win over the shadow tree's own declarations.
cssPartSpecificityHazard.concrete: table-footer styles the paginator arrows via sl-button fill=ghost. Setting the enabled colour to --sl-color-palette-grey-700 through the part ALSO overrode button.css's `button:is(:disabled)` rule, so the disabled arrows would have painted grey-700 instead of the disabled colour.
cssPartSpecificityHazard.whyItMatters: Both arrows ARE disabled in the design (3 rows at pageSize 25). No still image would have flagged this - the arrows would simply have been the wrong grey.
cssPartSpecificityHazard.fix: restate the disabled colour explicitly: --sl-color-foreground-disabled, which resolves to grey-300 #c8c8cf - byte-identical to the design's arrow colour.

environmentDefectsFound: npx eslint cannot run in this checkout at all: tools/eslint-plugin-slds imports eslint-plugin-lit, which is not installed. Lint is therefore NOT a gate any run in this batch has been passing.
npx prettier cannot parse any .ts using import attributes (`with { type: 'css' }`) - repo-wide, affecting every existing component, not just generated code.

typecheck.mjs parsed tsc output with a pattern that never matched, because tsc colourises even when piped: the pretty `file:line:col` form never matched a parser written for `file(line,col)`. It returned `clean` for every run in the batch until fixed. I reported the two grid.ts baseline errors as still present while the tool claimed they had vanished; the tool was wrong.

A SECOND, independent tsc artifact: while ANY file in the program has a syntax error, tsc skips semantic diagnostics program-wide, so the baseline errors disappear from the output and typecheck.mjs reports baselineErrorsNoLongerReported - which its own README defines as 'somebody edited shared code'. Nobody had. A sibling's in-progress file is enough to produce it.
